chapters.title: Chapter 1: Two Different Businesses Under One Name

lessons.title: Who Pays You: Families vs Businesses as Tenants

children.text: Meet two landlords in Hyderabad. Ramesh rents his Gachibowli 3BHK to a family for ₹42,000 a month. Eleven months in, the husband gets transferred to Pune and they leave with 30 days' notice. Sunita owns a 1,500 sq ft office unit in HITEC City leased to a pharma analytics firm that spent ₹40 lakh on interiors. That tenant has not missed a payment in four years and has no intention of moving. Same city, same asset class on paper, completely different relationships. This lesson is about the person, or the company, whose money actually turns a yield on paper into cash in your account.

body.text: In residential property you are renting to a household's salary. In commercial property you are renting to a business's cash flow. Your yield is only as reliable as the tenant paying it.

children.text: The Residential Tenant: A Household With a Salary

Most residential tenants in Indian cities are salaried professionals, young families and students. They choose a home for reasons that have little to do with you: commute time to the office, a school for the children, proximity to parents. That makes them easy to find in a job hub like Whitefield or Gachibowli, and just as easy to lose. A job change, a transfer, a marriage or a decision to finally buy their own flat, and they are gone.

markDefs.definition: A tenant background check submitted to the local police, required by many Indian city police departments before a tenant moves in. Skipping it can expose the owner to penalties.

children.text: Typical residential tenancies last one to three years, renewed through fresh 11-month agreements. Screening is personal rather than financial: employer ID, recent salary slips, a previous landlord's reference, and the
police verification
that many city police departments require.

Security deposits vary sharply by city. Bengaluru has long been known for deposits of up to 10 months' rent on homes, Mumbai commonly sees three to six months, and Delhi NCR often just one to two. The central Model Tenancy Act, 2021 proposes capping deposits at two months' rent for residential and six months for non-residential property, but it applies only in states that adopt it.

children.text: The Commercial Tenant: A Business With a Balance Sheet

A commercial tenant rents space because the space helps it make money: an IT firm needs desks, a pharmacy chain needs street frontage, an e-commerce company needs a warehouse near the highway. That changes everything about how they behave. They negotiate harder, they sign longer, and once settled they are much harder to dislodge.

markDefs.definition: Bare shell is space handed over with only the structure, walls and basic services; the tenant does the entire fit-out. Warm shell adds items like flooring, false ceiling, air-conditioning and washrooms, so the tenant needs less work to move in.

children.text: The reason is sunk cost. A tenant that has spent ₹2,000 to ₹3,000 per sq ft on air-conditioning, cabling, cabins and branding is not walking away over a small rent hike. Leaving means writing off that spend and paying for it all over again elsewhere. This is why commercial space is often let as
bare shell or warm shell
and why tenants who have fitted out a space tend to stay.

body.text: A tenant's cost of leaving is your best friend. The more a business has invested inside your unit, the safer your rent. A shop that put in ₹5 lakh of shelving is far less sticky than a bank branch that built a strongroom.

body.text: During the 2020 lockdowns, many small business tenants and co-working operators sought rent waivers or renegotiations, citing force majeure. Residential tenants mostly kept paying because they still needed a home. A higher-yielding tenant can turn into a zero-yielding one precisely when the economy is weakest.

children.text: How the Rent Reaches You

A residential tenant pays by UPI or bank transfer on the first of the month, in full, with no paperwork. If the monthly rent exceeds ₹50,000, an individual tenant must deduct TDS, currently 2%, and you claim it back when you file your return.

markDefs.definition: The GST a business pays on its purchases, including rent, which it can offset against the GST it collects on its own sales. For most businesses this makes GST on rent a pass-through cost.

children.text: A business tenant pays against an invoice. It deducts TDS, typically 10% on rent for buildings above ₹50,000 a month, and deposits it with the government in your PAN. If you are registered for GST, you add 18% GST to the invoice. Businesses rarely object, because they claim that GST back as
input tax credit

body.label: Cash in hand from a business tenant
body.context: On ₹1,00,000 monthly rent you receive ₹90,000 plus any GST billed; the ₹10,000 TDS is credited against your income tax, not lost.

children.text: The Lifecycle of a Commercial Lease
Commercial leases carry one feature residential landlords never deal with: a rent-free period at the start, while the tenant builds out the space. It lowers what you really earn over the lease.

body.title: A typical 9-year office lease in India

events.title: Term sheet and lease signed
events.description: Tenant pays the security deposit; lock-in, escalation and exit terms are fixed on paper.

events.title: Rent-free fit-out period
events.description: Tenant builds interiors. You earn no rent, though the tenant may already pay maintenance.

events.title: Rent starts
events.description: First invoice raised, TDS deducted, GST billed if applicable.

events.title: Lock-in ends, first escalation
events.description: Rent steps up, commonly 15%. The tenant can now exit with notice, so this is your first real renewal risk.

events.title: Second escalation
events.description: Another step-up. The tenant's fit-out is ageing, which can prompt a relocation decision.

events.title: Renewal or exit
events.description: Renegotiate at market rent, or prepare for vacancy and a fresh rent-free period for the next tenant.

body.latex: \text{Effective Monthly Rent} = \text{Headline Rent} \times \frac{\text{Lease Months} - \text{Rent-Free Months}}{\text{Lease Months}}
body.caption: Ignores escalations, to isolate the effect of rent-free months.

children.text: Take a headline rent of ₹1,00,000 a month on a 108-month lease with 3 rent-free months. You collect rent for 105 months, so the effective rent is ₹1,00,000 × 105 ÷ 108 = about ₹97,222 a month, roughly 2.8% below the headline. Brokers quote the headline. You should calculate the effective number.

body.title: Quick Check: Why Businesses Accept GST on Rent
body.question: Why do most business tenants not object when a landlord adds 18% GST to the rent invoice?
options: GST on rent is optional, so they can choose not to pay it
They can usually claim it back as input tax credit against the GST they collect
The landlord absorbs the GST out of the rent
GST only applies to residential rent
body.explanation: For most GST-registered businesses, GST paid on rent is offset against GST collected on their own sales, so it is largely a pass-through. Tenants that cannot fully claim input tax credit, such as some financial services businesses, negotiate harder on this point.

body.title: Calculate: Effective Rent on a HITEC City Office
body.prompt: An office in HITEC City is leased at a headline rent of ₹1,20,000 a month for 9 years (108 months), with 4 rent-free months for fit-out. Ignoring escalations, what is the effective monthly rent, to the nearest rupee?
body.explanation: Rent is collected for 108 minus 4 = 104 months. ₹1,20,000 × 104 ÷ 108 = ₹1,15,556 a month, about 3.7% below the headline.

body.title: Scenario: Higher Rent or Better Tenant?
body.scenario: You own a 1,000 sq ft office unit on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram. Two tenants want it. Tenant A is a startup founded 18 months ago offering ₹95 per sq ft a month, a 3-year lock-in and a 2-month deposit. Tenant B is a listed insurance company offering ₹82 per sq ft a month, a 5-year lock-in, a 6-month deposit and a 15% escalation every 3 years.
body.prompt: Which tenant would you choose, and why? Put numbers on it.
body.modelAnswer: Tenant B, in most cases. Tenant A pays ₹95,000 a month against Tenant B's ₹82,000, a premium of ₹13,000 a month or ₹1.56 lakh a year. If the startup shuts down and the unit sits empty for 9 months, you lose 9 × ₹95,000 = ₹8.55 lakh, which is more than five years of that premium, and its 2-month deposit covers only a fraction of it. Tenant B's 5-year lock-in and 6-month deposit protect your income far better, and after the first escalation its rent becomes ₹82,000 × 1.15 = ₹94,300, almost matching Tenant A anyway. There is also a resale angle: buyers of pre-leased property pay a higher price, meaning a lower cap rate, for a strong listed tenant than for a young startup. Tenant A only makes sense if you can verify strong funding and demand a larger deposit or a longer lock-in.

body.title: Tenant Screening Checklist
steps: Residential: collect employer ID, the last three salary slips and a previous landlord's contact
Residential: complete police verification before handing over keys
Commercial: check the company's registration and directors on the MCA portal
Commercial: if listed, review revenue, profit and debt trends on Screener.in
Commercial: ask how much the tenant plans to spend on fit-out; higher spend means a stickier tenant
Both: agree the deposit, notice period and escalation in writing before anyone moves in
Both: confirm who pays maintenance, property tax and utilities

Refundable money held by the landlord against unpaid rent or damage; norms range from 1 to 10 months' rent depending on city and property type.
Commercial space handed over with only the structure and basic services, leaving the full fit-out to the tenant.
Commercial space with flooring, ceiling, air-conditioning and washrooms already installed, needing less tenant fit-out.

points: Residential tenants rent from a salary and leave for life reasons you cannot control; commercial tenants rent because the space helps them earn money.
Fit-out spend is the biggest reason business tenants stay; the more they invest in your unit, the safer your rent.
Tenant credit strength ranges from MNCs and listed firms at the top to young startups and local businesses at the bottom.
Business tenants deduct TDS, usually 10%, and pay GST on top if you are registered, which they typically claim back as input tax credit.
Rent-free fit-out months lower your effective rent, so always calculate it instead of trusting the headline.
A higher rent from a weaker tenant is often worse than a lower rent from a strong one once vacancy risk is priced in.

body.text: Deposit norms, fit-out costs, TDS rates and GST thresholds in this lesson are indicative as of 2026 and vary by city, property and individual circumstances. Confirm current tax treatment with a qualified tax professional. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy or lease any property.
